title: India's forex reserves fall $14.2 billion to $705 billion, lowest in nearly three months
dek: RBI data show lower gold and foreign currency holdings in a week when the rupee weakened to 94.24 a dollar.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $14.2 billion to $705.34 billion in the week ended 13 November, their lowest level in nearly three months, according to Reserve Bank of India data released on Friday, as reported. The fall reversed a gain of $2.49 billion the previous week, when the reserves stood at $719.55 billion.

Foreign currency assets, the largest component, fell by $7.90 billion to $583.45 billion, and gold reserves by $6.18 billion to $98.61 billion, according to the data. Special drawing rights with the International Monetary Fund fell by $93 million to $18.52 billion and India's reserve position with the IMF by $33 million to $4.76 billion.

The RBI does not explain weekly moves. Changes in the dollar value of other currencies and of gold move the total even when the central bank does not trade, and reports differ on how much of this fall reflects revaluation and how much the RBI's dollar sales to support the rupee, which weakened about 0.3% to 94.24 a dollar during the week. The rupee has since recovered, closing at 92.67 on 20 November, its strongest level since April.

The reserves are about $80 billion below their record of $785.71 billion in the week ended 4 September, set after banks raised $133 billion through a concessional swap window for non-resident Indians' foreign currency deposits. The next weekly figures are due on Friday, 27 November.
